-- Zehn has no loops: iteration is recursion (or list.map / list.fold).
-- Every run has a fuel budget and a call-depth limit (SPEC section 13), so a wrong base case
-- becomes a diagnostic (E0801 / E0802) instead of a hang.
fn gcd(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
  intent "greatest common divisor by Euclid's algorithm"
  requires a >= 0
  requires b >= 0
  ensures out >= 0
  example gcd(12, 18) == 6
  example gcd(7, 0) == 7
do
  if b == 0 then
    return a
  else
    return gcd(b, a % b)
  end if
end fn

fn sum_to(n: Int) -> Int
  intent "1 + 2 + ... + n, by plain recursion (depth n)"
  requires n >= 0
  example sum_to(0) == 0
  example sum_to(1000) == 500500
do
  if n == 0 then
    return 0
  else
    return n + sum_to(n - 1)
  end if
end fn

fn fib_from(a: Int, b: Int, n: Int) -> Int
  intent "the value n steps along the Fibonacci walk that starts at the pair (a, b)"
  requires n >= 0
  example fib_from(0, 1, 10) == 55
do
  if n == 0 then
    return a
  else
    return fib_from(b, a + b, n - 1)
  end if
end fn

fn fib(n: Int) -> Int
  intent "n-th Fibonacci number in linear time (the naive double recursion would exhaust fuel)"
  requires n >= 0
  example fib(50) == 12586269025
do
  return fib_from(0, 1, n)
end fn

fn sign(n: Int) -> Int
  intent "-1, 0 or 1; every path returns, which `zehn check` verifies statically (E0310)"
  example sign(-9) == -1
  example sign(0) == 0
  example sign(4) == 1
do
  if n < 0 then
    return -1
  else
    if n == 0 then
      return 0
    else
      return 1
    end if
  end if
end fn
